guidance: Keep food scraps separate from dry recyclables. Use the local wet-waste collection or an approved home/community composting system. Avoid mixing plastic, glass or chemicals with compost feedstock.
keywords: food scraps fruit peels vegetable peels compost wet waste

guidance: Place unavoidable cooked-food leftovers in the wet-waste stream according to local collection rules. Keep packaging, foil, cutlery and plastic separate. Do not put hot oil or chemicals into compost.
keywords: leftover food cooked rice curry wet waste

guidance: Keep clean, dry paper separate from wet waste. Flatten or bundle it and send it through the local dry-waste collection or authorised recycler. Paper contaminated with food or oil may not be accepted for recycling.
keywords: newspaper office paper clean paper recycle dry waste

guidance: Flatten clean and dry cardboard boxes. Remove excess tape or plastic where practical and keep them dry for the local dry-waste collector or authorised recycler.
keywords: cardboard carton packaging box recycle

guidance: Empty the bottle, keep it reasonably clean and place it in the locally accepted dry-recyclable stream. Do not burn plastic. Follow local instructions for caps and labels.
keywords: PET bottle plastic bottle recycle dry waste

guidance: Keep wrappers separate from wet waste. Multi-layered or soiled wrappers may not be accepted by ordinary recyclers. Follow local collection guidance and avoid littering or burning.
keywords: chips packet snack wrapper multilayer plastic

guidance: Empty the container and keep it separate from wet waste. Do not put broken glass loose into a bag; wrap it securely and label it so sanitation workers are protected. Check local collection rules.
keywords: glass bottle jar broken glass recycle

guidance: Empty and, where safe, rinse the can. Keep it with dry recyclables for local collection. Handle sharp edges carefully and do not crush cans by hand.
keywords: aluminium tin steel can metal recycling

category: Separate collection; do not pour into drains
guidance: Never pour used cooking oil into a sink or storm drain. Let it cool, store it in a sealed container and check local municipal or authorised collection arrangements. Do not mix it with compost unless local guidance explicitly permits it.
keywords: cooking oil grease drain used oil

guidance: Keep batteries out of wet and ordinary dry waste. Store safely away from heat and children, avoid puncturing or crushing them, and use an authorised battery collection or take-back channel. Battery type matters.
keywords: AA battery cell household battery hazardous waste

guidance: Do not place phones in household wet or dry waste. Delete personal data, remove accounts where possible, and hand the device to an authorised e-waste collection point, producer take-back channel or recycler.
keywords: old phone smartphone electronics e waste

guidance: Keep electronic equipment separate from municipal household waste. Back up and erase personal data, remove accounts and use an authorised e-waste collection or producer take-back channel.
keywords: laptop computer keyboard monitor e waste

guidance: Do not break fluorescent lamps. Keep them protected from breakage and use an authorised collection channel for lamps or e-waste. If one breaks, keep people away and follow local public-health guidance for safe cleanup.
keywords: CFL tube light fluorescent bulb mercury

guidance: Do not flush medicines or mix them with compost. Keep them in original packaging where practical and ask a pharmacy, healthcare provider or local authority about an approved take-back or disposal route.
keywords: expired tablets medicine pharmaceutical waste

guidance: Wrap sanitary waste securely and follow the municipal collection instructions. Do not mix it with loose recyclables or compost. Do not burn it in the open.
keywords: sanitary napkin diaper hygiene waste

category: Wet or reject waste; local rules vary
guidance: Food-soiled tissues are generally not suitable for paper recycling. Follow local wet-waste or reject-waste instructions; keep them out of clean-paper recyclables.
keywords: dirty tissue paper towel food stained

item: Garden leaves and small plant trimmings
guidance: Keep leaves and plant trimmings separate from plastic and other dry waste. Use municipal green-waste collection or composting where available. Large branches may need a separate collection service.
keywords: leaves garden waste grass biodegradable compost

guidance: Do not pour leftover chemicals into drains, soil or regular compost. Keep the container closed and labelled, avoid mixing chemicals, and contact the local authority or authorised hazardous-waste handler for instructions.
keywords: paint thinner pesticide chemical container hazardous

guidance: If wearable, consider repair, donation or reuse. Clean, dry unusable textiles may be accepted by textile collection programmes. Do not assume every textile is recyclable through household dry-waste collection.
keywords: old clothes fabric textile donation reuse

guidance: Ceramics are not the same as recyclable glass bottles. Wrap broken pieces securely, label them to prevent injuries and follow local reject-waste instructions.
keywords: ceramic cup mug plates crockery broken
